ruling.recommended_action: Refund the $6.61 cancellation fee to the rider as a Ryde voucher (NS-7) and send the driver's "I'm Here" tap 600 m from the pickup to Ryde account review for cancellation/waiting-button abuse + flag_account
ruling.reasoning:
Safety screen: the chat [F8][F9][F10], the complaint and the driver statement [F12] contain no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation, and the dispute type is no-show, not safety. Nothing to escalate on SAFE-1/SAFE-2.

Branch: the $6.61 cancellation fee is only chargeable through NS-0. Here cancelled_by = driver and the driver asserts a rider no-show [F3][F12], so NS-1 governs.

NS-1 requires all of (i) an "I'm Here" tap or platform-arrival confirmation, (ii) the driver within the pickup radius at the tap, and (iii) more than 3 continuous minutes waiting inside the radius thereafter. (i) holds: he tapped "I'm Here" at 12:06:15 [F5]. (ii) fails: at the tap he was 600 m from the pickup [F5], his closest approach in the whole trip was 599 m [F1], and the platform's driver_arrived_at is null [F4]. (iii) also fails: he stayed within 200 m for 0 s after the tap [F5]; he was stationary 12:05:55–12:09:25 600 m away [F2]. His post-trip statement of waiting at the pickup [F12] is a claim, and GPS/timeline records override it.

Per NS-2, the $6.61 no-show fee does not stand and is refunded in full ($6.61). Because the driver pressed "I'm Here" while GPS placed him well outside the pickup radius (>200 m) [F5], NS-2's second limb applies: the case is additionally flagged to Ryde account review for abuse of the cancellation/waiting button. Flag is supported by the profile counter (1 upheld no-show dispute) [F17], which is corroborating only, not the basis of the finding. Traffic facts are irrelevant: no incidents [F14] and a moderate band [F13] do not bear on a fee that fails NS-1 outright. Refund to be issued as a Ryde voucher per NS-7.

rejected_claims.reason: Driver's post-trip statement that he waited >3 min at the pickup is a claim contradicted by system records: GPS shows his closest approach was 599 m and that he was stationary 600 m away the whole time [F1][F2], and the platform never recorded him at the pickup point [F4]. Under NS-1 (ii) and the system-records-over-statements rule, the claim fails.
Driver's chat 'I'm here already' at 12:06 is falsified by GPS: at the tap moment and throughout he was 600 m from the pickup [F1][F2][F5]; the rider's reply confirms no car was at the pickup [F9].
